pack.description: Read in Daily Life — original notices, emails, messages, schedules and web pages.
pack.copyright_policy: Original synthetic content. No operational ETS item copied.

stimulus.title: Library Study Rooms — Exam Week
stimulus.body: From Monday through Friday, group study rooms may be reserved for up to two hours per day. Reservations must be made online at least 30 minutes before use. Rooms left empty for more than 15 minutes may be reassigned. Individual students may use an unreserved room, but groups with a valid booking have priority. On Saturday and Sunday, rooms will be available on a first-come, first-served basis.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of the notice?
options: To announce special study-room rules during exam week
To explain why the library will close early
To recruit students to manage study rooms
To advertise newly constructed rooms
questions.explanation: The title and every sentence describe how rooms may be used during exam week; nothing mentions closing, recruiting or new rooms.

questions.stem: What can happen if a reserved room remains unused for more than 15 minutes?
options: The reservation automatically extends
Another group may receive the room
The student loses library privileges
The room becomes unavailable for the day
questions.explanation: "May be reassigned" means the room can be given to someone else.

questions.stem: What is different on the weekend?
options: Students may reserve rooms for longer periods
Only groups may use the rooms
Advance reservations are not used
The library charges for room use
questions.explanation: "First-come, first-served" implies that no bookings are taken: whoever arrives first gets the room.

stimulus.body:
Dear residents,

To complete repairs to the main pipe, water to Elmwood Hall will be turned off on Thursday from 9 a.m. until approximately 2 p.m. Showers in the Fitness Center will remain open to residents with a valid ID during this time. If the work is finished early, we will not send a further message; simply check whether your taps are working. Please do not report the outage to the maintenance hotline unless water has not returned by 4 p.m.

Thank you for your patience,
Housing Services

questions.stem: What are residents advised to do if they need a shower on Thursday morning?
options: Call the maintenance hotline
Use the facilities at the Fitness Center
Wait until Housing Services sends an update
Request a temporary room in another hall
questions.explanation: The email states that Fitness Center showers stay open to residents with an ID.

questions.stem: What can be inferred about the end of the repairs?
options: Residents will receive a second email when water returns
The exact finishing time is not certain
The work will continue until 4 p.m.
The repairs have already been delayed once
questions.explanation: "Approximately 2 p.m." and "if the work is finished early" show the end time is uncertain. No second email will be sent.

messages.text: Just saw Dr. Okafor moved the lab report deadline to Monday.
Great, so we don't need to meet tomorrow?
We still should. The new rubric wants a second data set, and the lab is closed all weekend.
I can't make it before noon. Could we do 1 o'clock instead of 10?
Works for me. I'll book bench 3.

questions.stem: Why does Priya think the group should still meet tomorrow?
options: The deadline has been moved earlier
Additional data must be collected while the lab is open
Dr. Okafor wants to see a draft of the report
Tom has not finished his part of the analysis
questions.explanation: She mentions the requirement for a second data set and that the lab is closed during the weekend, so tomorrow is the last chance.

questions.stem: What will Tom most likely do next?
options: Ask Dr. Okafor for an extension
Reserve a workspace in the lab for 1 o'clock
Cancel the meeting with Mei
Collect the data alone at 10 o'clock
questions.explanation: Tom agrees to Mei's 1 o'clock suggestion and says he will book bench 3.

questions.stem: In Tom's first message, what does he imply?
options: He assumes the later deadline makes the meeting unnecessary
He is annoyed that the deadline has changed
He has already finished his section of the report
He did not know there was a lab report
questions.explanation: "Great, so we don't need to meet tomorrow?" shows he infers that more time means no meeting is needed — an assumption Priya corrects.

stimulus.title: Campus Shuttle — Winter Break Service
stimulus.footer: All routes are suspended on December 25 and January 1. Real-time locations are shown in the CampusGo app.

questions.stem: A student wants to travel on the North Loop on a Saturday during winter break. What should the student expect?
options: A bus every 20 minutes
A bus every hour
No bus on that route
Service only until 5 p.m.
questions.explanation: The weekend column for the North Loop says "No service".

questions.stem: Which route operates the same timetable every day of the week except holidays?
options: North Loop
Medical Campus Express
Downtown Link
None of the routes
questions.explanation: Only the Downtown Link has identical weekday and weekend entries (hourly, 9 a.m.–5 p.m.).

stimulus.title: Graduate Writing Center — Appointment Policy
stimulus.body: Consultations last 50 minutes and may be booked up to two weeks in advance. Each student may hold one future appointment at a time; a new booking becomes possible once the current one has taken place. Please upload your draft at least 24 hours beforehand so that your consultant can read it. If you upload later, the session will still go ahead, but it will focus on the sections you choose to read aloud. Two missed appointments without notice in a semester will suspend online booking; you may then use drop-in hours only.

questions.stem: According to the page, what happens if a draft is uploaded less than a day before the session?
options: The appointment is cancelled automatically
The consultant reviews only the parts the student reads during the session
The student must wait two weeks for a new appointment
The session is shortened to 25 minutes
questions.explanation: Late uploads do not cancel the session; it focuses on the sections the student reads aloud.

questions.stem: A student has an appointment next Tuesday and wants to book another for the following week. What is true?
options: The student can book both now
The student must use drop-in hours instead
The student can book the second appointment only after Tuesday's session
The student must upload both drafts in advance
questions.explanation: Only one future appointment is allowed; a new booking becomes possible once the current one has taken place.

questions.stem: The word "suspend" in the passage is closest in meaning to
options: delay
temporarily stop
permanently cancel
investigate
questions.explanation: Online booking is stopped for a period, and drop-in hours remain available — a temporary stop, not a permanent cancellation.

stimulus.title: Room available — Maple Street (shared house)
stimulus.body: Furnished room in a quiet four-person house, a 10-minute walk from campus. Rent is $640 per month, including internet and water; electricity is split equally among housemates. The lease runs from September to May, but subletting over the winter break is permitted with notice. No pets, as one housemate has allergies. We are looking for a graduate student or a final-year undergraduate. Viewings on weekday evenings only — message Daniel.

questions.stem: Which cost is NOT included in the monthly rent?
options: Internet
Water
Electricity
Furniture
questions.explanation: Electricity is split among housemates separately; internet and water are included and the room is furnished.

questions.stem: Who would most likely be considered for the room?
options: A first-year student with a cat
A master's student who plans to go home in December
A professor looking for a family apartment
A student who can only visit on Saturday
questions.explanation: Graduate students are welcome and subletting over winter break is allowed. Pets are excluded, and viewings are on weekday evenings only.

stimulus.title: Memo — Department of Chemistry
stimulus.body: Several students have asked why their Lab 4 scores differ across sections. Having reviewed a sample, we found that some sections deducted points for missing units while others did not. Going forward, please apply the rubric exactly as written: missing units cost one point per table, not per value. Rather than regrading every report, we will adjust affected scores automatically. Students who believe an error remains should contact their own TA, not the course coordinator, by Friday.

questions.stem: Why was the memo written?
options: To announce that Lab 4 has been cancelled
To correct inconsistent grading across sections
To introduce a new rubric for future labs
To ask teaching assistants to regrade every report
questions.explanation: Sections applied the unit deduction differently; the memo clarifies the rule. It explicitly rejects regrading every report.

questions.stem: A report has three values without units, all in the same table. How many points should be deducted for missing units?
options: None
One
Two
Three
questions.explanation: The rule is one point per table, not per value.

questions.stem: What can be inferred about the course coordinator?
options: The coordinator wrote the original rubric incorrectly
The coordinator does not want to handle individual score complaints
The coordinator will regrade all the reports personally
The coordinator teaches one of the lab sections
questions.explanation: Students are told to contact their own TA, "not the course coordinator", which implies the coordinator is not processing individual queries.

stimulus.title: Riverside Café — Weekday Lunch
stimulus.footer: Show a valid student ID for 10% off items not already discounted.

questions.stem: A student with a nut allergy who does not eat meat wants lunch on a Tuesday. Which item is the safest choice?
options: Soup of the day
Grilled chicken wrap
Lentil salad bowl
Any item with the meal deal
questions.explanation: The wrap contains nuts and meat; the soup is vegetarian only on Mon/Wed/Fri. The lentil bowl is vegan.

questions.stem: What is true about the student discount?
options: It can be added to the meal deal
It applies only between 11:30 and 1:30
It cannot be combined with the meal deal
It is available only on weekends
questions.explanation: The discount applies to items "not already discounted"; the meal deal is itself a discount.

stimulus.title: Course Withdrawal Request — Instructions
stimulus.body: Use this form to withdraw from a single course after the add/drop period. Withdrawals submitted by the end of week 8 appear as "W" on your transcript and do not affect your grade point average. After week 8, a withdrawal requires documented medical or family circumstances and the approval of the Dean's Office. International students must also obtain a signature from an immigration advisor, since dropping below full-time enrollment may affect visa status. Tuition is not refunded for withdrawals after the add/drop period.

questions.stem: What happens to a student who withdraws from a course in week 6?
options: The student receives a partial tuition refund
The course is removed from the transcript entirely
A "W" appears, but the grade point average is unaffected
The student needs approval from the Dean's Office
questions.explanation: Before the end of week 8, withdrawals show as "W" without affecting the GPA. Dean's approval is only needed after week 8.

questions.stem: Why must international students consult an immigration advisor?
options: Because their tuition is calculated differently
Because a reduced course load could have consequences for their visa
Because the Dean's Office does not process their forms
Because they cannot withdraw after week 8
questions.explanation: The form explains that falling below full-time enrollment may affect visa status.

questions.stem: The form suggests that the add/drop period
options: ends after week 8
is the only time a full refund is possible
does not apply to international students
requires a medical certificate
questions.explanation: Tuition is not refunded for withdrawals after add/drop, which implies refunds are only possible during it.

stimulus.title: Campus Sustainability Office
stimulus.body: Update on the reusable-cup pilot: in its first month, disposable cup use in the two participating cafés fell by 41%. That's encouraging, but not quite the whole story — some of you told us you simply bought drinks elsewhere to avoid the deposit. So from next month, all six campus cafés will take part, and the deposit will drop from $2 to $1. Return points will also move closer to the lecture halls. Keep the feedback coming!

questions.stem: Why does the office say the 41% figure is "not quite the whole story"?
options: The figure was calculated incorrectly
Some customers avoided the scheme by going to other cafés
Disposable cups were still given away for free
Only two cafés reported their results
questions.explanation: Part of the decrease came from students buying drinks elsewhere, so the figure overstates the real reduction.

questions.stem: Which change is intended to address the problem described in the post?
options: Publishing monthly results online
Including every campus café in the scheme
Charging customers for disposable cups
Selling reusable cups at a discount
questions.explanation: If all cafés participate, students can no longer avoid the deposit by switching café. (The lower deposit and closer return points help too, but those options are not listed.)

stimulus.title: Bicycle Storage Room — Temporary Closure
stimulus.body: The indoor bicycle room in Hadley Hall will be closed from Monday, March 4, to Friday, March 8, while the floor is repainted. Please remove your bicycle by Sunday evening. Any bicycle still inside on Monday morning will be moved to the outdoor racks behind the building, and the residence office cannot accept responsibility for damage or theft there. The room will reopen on Saturday, March 9. Your current access card will continue to work.

questions.stem: What will happen to a bicycle left in the room on Monday morning?
options: It will be locked inside until Saturday
It will be taken to the residence office
It will be removed and its owner fined
It will be placed on the racks outside
questions.explanation: The notice says any bicycle still inside "will be moved to the outdoor racks behind the building".

questions.stem: What does the notice suggest about the outdoor racks?
options: They are less secure than the indoor room
They will also be repainted that week
They can only be used with an access card
They are reserved for residents of another hall
questions.explanation: The office "cannot accept responsibility for damage or theft there", which implies bicycles are at greater risk outside.

stimulus.body:
Dear tenants,

A technician will visit on Thursday between 9 a.m. and noon to replace the faulty valve on the main heating unit. The heating and hot water will be switched off during the work, which should take about two hours.

The technician needs to enter each apartment for a few minutes to check the radiators. If you will not be at home, please leave your key with Mr. Osei in apartment 1 or let me know that I may use the building's spare key.

I apologize for the short notice. The part arrived earlier than expected, and I did not want you to spend another cold weekend.

Dana

questions.stem: Why did the property manager write this email?
options: To apologize for a repair that was carried out badly
To ask tenants to report problems with their radiators
To tell tenants about a repair and arrange access to their apartments
To explain why the heating cannot be repaired this week
questions.explanation: The email announces Thursday's repair and asks tenants who will be out to leave a key or allow use of the spare key.

questions.stem: What should a tenant who will be out on Thursday morning do?
options: Switch off their radiators before leaving for the morning
Phone the technician to arrange a visit later in the week
Leave the apartment door unlocked so the technician can enter
Give a key to a neighbor or allow the manager to use the spare key
questions.explanation: Tenants are asked to "leave your key with Mr. Osei in apartment 1 or let me know that I may use the building's spare key".

questions.stem: What can be inferred about the heating in the building?
options: It was installed only recently
It breaks down every winter
It works in some apartments but not in apartment 1
It has not been working properly for some time
questions.explanation: The manager did not want tenants "to spend another cold weekend", so they have already had at least one.

stimulus.title: Recreation Center — Evening Classes, Spring Term
stimulus.footer: Classes are free for students. Sign up online from 8 a.m. on the day of the class. If you miss two classes you signed up for, you cannot sign up again for two weeks.

questions.stem: Which class sets a requirement that participants must already meet?
options: Yoga Flow
Swim Technique
Indoor Climbing
Strength Circuit
questions.explanation: Only Swim Technique requires an existing ability: participants "must swim 100 m without stopping". Indoor Climbing is for beginners.

questions.stem: A student signed up for Yoga Flow and Strength Circuit last week but attended neither. What is the consequence?
options: The student must pay a fee for both classes
The student may only join beginners' classes
The student is blocked from signing up for two weeks
The student loses access to the recreation center
questions.explanation: The footer states that missing two classes you signed up for means "you cannot sign up again for two weeks".

messages.text: Inspection is Friday at 10. The landlord's checklist says oven, fridge and bathroom have to be spotless or we lose part of the deposit.
I can do the bathroom tonight. The oven is beyond me though, last time I made it worse.
Fine, I'll take the oven if someone else empties the fridge. Half of what's in there isn't even mine.
That would be my half. I'm back Thursday afternoon, I'll deal with it then. Can someone buy oven cleaner? We're out.
On it. I'm passing the store anyway.

questions.stem: Who will clean the oven?
options: Leila
Marco
Jun
The landlord
questions.explanation: Leila writes, "I'll take the oven if someone else empties the fridge", and Jun agrees to deal with the fridge.

questions.stem: What does Jun mean by "That would be my half"?
options: Jun has already cleaned half of the fridge
Jun wants to pay half of the deposit
The food Leila mentioned belongs to Jun
Jun thinks the fridge should be shared more fairly
questions.explanation: Leila says half the food in the fridge "isn't even mine"; Jun admits that it is Jun's.

questions.stem: What will Marco most likely do next?
options: Start cleaning the oven
Empty the fridge before Thursday
Buy oven cleaner on his way
Ask the landlord to change the inspection time
questions.explanation: Jun asks someone to buy oven cleaner and Marco answers, "On it. I'm passing the store anyway."

stimulus.title: NorthLine Mobile — Statement for April
stimulus.footer: The late payment charge is removed automatically if this statement is paid in full by the due date. To avoid extra data charges, you can change to the 30 GB plan ($33.00 per month) at any time in the app.

rows: Extra data (3 GB over the limit)

questions.stem: How much will the customer finally pay for April if the total is paid on May 6?
questions.explanation: Paying in full by May 10 removes the $5.00 late charge automatically, so $38.00 becomes $33.00.

questions.stem: For a customer who uses 23 GB every month, what would be the effect of changing to the 30 GB plan?
options: The monthly cost before the discount would rise by $5.00
The student discount would no longer apply
The monthly cost before the discount would fall by $4.00
The customer would still pay for 3 GB of extra data
questions.explanation: The current plan plus extra data costs $28.00 + $9.00 = $37.00; the 30 GB plan costs $33.00, which is $4.00 less.

stimulus.title: Student Health Center — Flu Vaccination
stimulus.body:
Free flu vaccinations are available to all enrolled students from October 7. No appointment is needed on Tuesdays and Thursdays between 1 p.m. and 4 p.m.; on other days, please book online. Bring your student card.

You should postpone your vaccination if you currently have a fever. A mild cold is not a reason to wait. Students who have had a serious reaction to a previous vaccine must speak to a nurse first.

Protection develops about two weeks after the injection, so we recommend coming before the end of October, when cases on campus usually begin to rise.

questions.stem: Which student can simply walk in and receive a vaccination without booking?
options: A student who arrives at 2 p.m. on a Thursday
A student who arrives at 10 a.m. on a Tuesday
A student who arrives at 3 p.m. on a Friday
A student who has forgotten their student card
questions.explanation: Walk-in vaccination is offered "on Tuesdays and Thursdays between 1 p.m. and 4 p.m."; other times need a booking.

questions.stem: Why does the page recommend being vaccinated before the end of October?
options: Because the supply of vaccine is limited
Because the center closes in November
So that protection is in place before infections become common
So that students avoid long lines later in the term
questions.explanation: Protection takes about two weeks to develop, and cases "usually begin to rise" at the end of October.

questions.stem: The word "postpone" on the page is closest in meaning to
options: cancel
repeat
delay
confirm
questions.explanation: Students with a fever should have the vaccination later, not give it up entirely.

stimulus.title: Peer Tutors Wanted — Learning Commons
stimulus.body: The Learning Commons is hiring peer tutors for statistics, organic chemistry and academic writing. Tutors work four to eight hours a week, mostly in the late afternoon, and are paid $17 an hour. You must have earned at least an A− in the course you wish to tutor and be recommended by a faculty member. Previous teaching experience is welcome but not expected: all new tutors complete ten hours of paid training before meeting students. Apply by September 12 through the student employment portal.

questions.stem: According to the advertisement, what must every applicant have?
options: Experience of teaching or tutoring
A completed training certificate
A recommendation from a faculty member
Availability in the morning
questions.explanation: Applicants must "be recommended by a faculty member"; experience is "welcome but not expected", and training comes after hiring.

questions.stem: What can be inferred about the ten hours of training?
options: Tutors receive wages while they complete it
It must be finished before applying
It replaces the faculty recommendation
It is only for tutors of academic writing
questions.explanation: The advertisement describes it as "ten hours of paid training" completed by all new tutors.

stimulus.title: Memo — Teaching Assistants, Introductory Biology
stimulus.body:
Thank you for returning the first midterm so promptly. Several students nevertheless pointed out that comments on the short-answer questions varied considerably from one section to another, and a comparison of sample papers confirmed it.

For the second midterm, we will therefore grade differently. Instead of each of you grading your own sections, every assistant will grade one question across all sections. This will take longer, so the deadline for returning papers is extended from five to eight working days. We will meet on the Monday after the exam to agree on the criteria before anyone begins.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of the memo?
options: To announce a new grading procedure and the reason for it
To criticize assistants who graded the first midterm late
To ask assistants to write more detailed comments
To inform assistants that the second midterm has been postponed
questions.explanation: The memo explains that feedback varied between sections and that, "therefore", each assistant will now grade one question across all sections.

questions.stem: What problem is the new procedure mainly intended to solve?
options: Different assistants applying different standards to the same question
Assistants taking too long to return graded papers to students
Students finding the short-answer questions too hard to answer
Each assistant being responsible for too many sections at once
questions.explanation: Comments "varied considerably from one section to another"; having one person grade each question for everyone removes that variation.

questions.stem: What will the assistants do on the Monday after the exam?
options: Return the graded papers to students
Compare sample papers from the first midterm
Agree on how answers should be assessed
Divide the sections among themselves
questions.explanation: They "will meet on the Monday after the exam to agree on the criteria before anyone begins".

meta.label: Subject
meta.value: Re: Extension for the policy brief

stimulus.body:
Dear Amara,

Thank you for explaining your situation, and I am sorry to hear about the difficulties with your internship schedule.

I am reluctant to move the deadline for one student when the brief was announced six weeks ago. That said, I would rather read careful work than rushed work. If you send me your outline and your list of sources by Friday, so that I can see the project is under way, you may submit the final version on the following Wednesday instead of Monday. Please do not treat this as a precedent for the final paper.

Best,
H. Solberg

questions.stem: What must Amara do in order to receive the extension?
options: Submit the complete brief by Friday
Provide proof of her internship schedule
Show by Friday that she has already begun the work
Agree to a lower grade for late work
questions.explanation: The extension is conditional: she must send "your outline and your list of sources by Friday, so that I can see the project is under way".

questions.stem: Which statement best describes the professor's attitude toward the request?
options: He is pleased to help and encourages similar requests
He refuses but offers advice instead
He is indifferent to when the brief is submitted
He grants it with some hesitation and sets limits
questions.explanation: He is "reluctant to move the deadline" yet allows it on conditions, and adds that it is not "a precedent for the final paper".

stimulus.title: Travel Reimbursement Request — Instructions
stimulus.body:
Complete this form within 30 days of returning from your trip. Requests received after that date require written approval from the department head and may be refused.

Attach original receipts for every expense above $25. Meals are reimbursed at a fixed daily rate, so meal receipts are not required. Travel by private car is reimbursed per kilometer; fuel receipts are therefore not accepted. If a conference fee was paid directly by the department, do not list it here.

Reimbursement is normally paid within three weeks. Incomplete forms are returned to the applicant, and the three-week period begins again when the corrected form arrives.

questions.stem: For which of the following must a receipt be attached?
options: A $30 restaurant dinner
A $60 train ticket
$40 of fuel for a private car
A conference fee paid by the department
questions.explanation: Receipts are needed "for every expense above $25", but meals use a fixed rate, fuel receipts "are not accepted", and department-paid fees are not listed at all.

questions.stem: Why are fuel receipts not accepted for travel by private car?
options: Because fuel is considered a personal expense
Because private cars may not be used for university travel
Because the payment is calculated from the distance driven
Because fuel costs are included in the daily meal rate
questions.explanation: Car travel "is reimbursed per kilometer", so the amount of fuel bought is irrelevant: "fuel receipts are therefore not accepted".

questions.stem: A student submits the form 20 days after a trip but forgets one receipt. What will happen?
options: The request will need the approval of the department head
The request will be refused
The missing expense will be reimbursed at a fixed rate
The form will be sent back and the payment period will restart later
questions.explanation: "Incomplete forms are returned to the applicant, and the three-week period begins again when the corrected form arrives."

stimulus.title: Chemistry Building — Fume Hood Inspection
stimulus.body:
The annual inspection of fume hoods on the third floor will take place on Wednesday, November 13. Each hood will be out of service for approximately forty minutes while airflow is measured. Inspectors will work from room 301 toward room 318, so laboratories at the far end of the corridor should expect their inspection in the afternoon.

No experiment involving volatile solvents may be left running in a hood on that day. Hoods that fail the test will be labeled and must not be used until repaired; in previous years, repairs have taken up to two weeks. Researchers with time-sensitive work should arrange in advance to share a hood on another floor.

questions.stem: A researcher works in room 317. What should she expect on November 13?
options: Her hood will be out of service for the whole day
Her hood will be tested before the one in room 301
Her laboratory will be closed during the inspection
Her hood will probably be tested later in the day
questions.explanation: Inspectors move "from room 301 toward room 318", so rooms "at the far end of the corridor should expect their inspection in the afternoon".

questions.stem: Why does the notice mention that repairs "have taken up to two weeks"?
options: To apologize for the slow work of the repair service
To show that most hoods fail the inspection
To explain why some researchers should plan to use a hood elsewhere
To justify moving the inspection to an earlier date
questions.explanation: A failed hood could be unusable for weeks, which is why those "with time-sensitive work should arrange in advance to share a hood on another floor".

messages.text: Slides are due at noon tomorrow. I've done the introduction and the survey results. Tomás, how's the theory section coming?
Getting there. I've read the three articles, I just haven't quite turned them into slides yet.
So... nothing on the slides.
Not as such. But the notes are solid. Give me until 9 tomorrow morning?
9 leaves me three hours to make everything look consistent. I suppose that's workable. But please, bullet points, not paragraphs this time.
Understood. Short and sharp.

questions.stem: What does Tomás mean when he writes "Not as such"?
options: He disagrees that the slides are his responsibility
He has made slides but is not satisfied with them
He admits that he has not yet made any slides
He does not understand what Priya is asking
questions.explanation: Priya concludes "nothing on the slides"; "Not as such" is a softened way of saying she is right, and he points to his notes instead.

questions.stem: How does Priya respond to Tomás's request for more time?
options: She refuses because noon is too close
She offers to write the theory section herself
She agrees gladly and extends the deadline further
She accepts it without enthusiasm and adds a condition
questions.explanation: "I suppose that's workable" is reluctant agreement, followed by the demand for "bullet points, not paragraphs this time".

questions.stem: What can be inferred about a previous piece of work by Tomás?
options: He submitted it after the deadline
He relied on too few sources
His slides contained too much continuous text
His section did not match the survey results
questions.explanation: Priya asks for "bullet points, not paragraphs this time", implying that last time he wrote paragraphs.

stimulus.title: University Library — Interlibrary Loans
stimulus.body:
If the library does not hold an item you need, we can usually borrow it from a partner institution. Books typically arrive within five to ten working days; scanned articles and chapters are generally delivered by email within three.

Loan periods are set by the lending library, not by us, and are often shorter than our own. Renewals are possible only if the lender agrees, so please request one at least four days before the due date. Items marked "library use only" must be read in the reading room and cannot be taken home under any circumstances.

The service is free for up to twenty requests per academic year. Beyond that, a charge of $6 per item applies.

questions.stem: Who decides how long a borrowed book may be kept?
options: The student's home library
The student's department
The library that owns the book
The reading room staff
questions.explanation: "Loan periods are set by the lending library, not by us."

questions.stem: A doctoral student needs one chapter of a book as quickly as possible. What would the page lead her to do?
options: Request the book and read it in the reading room
Request a scan of the chapter instead of the whole book
Ask for a renewal four days in advance
Pay the $6 charge for faster delivery
questions.explanation: Scanned chapters are "delivered by email within three" working days, whereas books take "five to ten".

stimulus.title: Student Union — Election Results
stimulus.body: Thank you to the 2,140 students who voted in this year's union elections. That is 19% of those eligible, up from 14% last spring, and the highest figure since online voting was introduced. We are pleased, though hardly satisfied: four out of five students still had no say in who represents them. Turnout was highest in the School of Engineering (31%), where candidates visited every first-year lecture, and lowest among graduate students (8%). Next year we will ask all candidates to do the same, and we will hold a separate information evening for graduate students.

questions.stem: Why does the post state that "four out of five students still had no say"?
options: To stress that the improved turnout remains low
To blame students who did not vote
To suggest that the election result is not valid
To show that online voting has failed
questions.explanation: The union is "pleased, though hardly satisfied"; restating 19% as four in five non-voters shows how much room remains.

questions.stem: What does the union believe contributed to the high turnout in Engineering?

The introduction of online voting
A separate information evening
Candidates speaking to students in their lectures
questions.explanation: Engineering is described as the school "where candidates visited every first-year lecture", and the union will "ask all candidates to do the same".

options: Voting in the union elections
Holding an information evening
Publishing the turnout figures
Visiting every first-year lecture
questions.explanation: "The same" points back to what the Engineering candidates did: they "visited every first-year lecture".

stimulus.body:
Dear Mr. Mensah,

We have considered your request to move from Aldrich House to a single room. As you know, room changes during the term are approved only where a resident's health or safety is concerned, and noise from neighboring rooms, however frustrating, does not ordinarily meet that standard.

We would not want to leave matters there. The resident adviser for your floor has been asked to speak with the students concerned this week. Should the situation be unchanged after fourteen days, write to us again, mentioning this message, and your request will be reviewed without the usual form. Single rooms for next term may in any case be requested from November 1.

questions.stem: What is the main message of the email?
options: The request has been approved and will take effect in fourteen days
The request cannot be considered until November 1
The request is refused for now, but steps are being taken and it may be reconsidered
The request was incomplete and must be submitted again on the usual form
questions.explanation: Noise "does not ordinarily meet that standard", yet the office will not "leave matters there": an adviser will intervene and the request "will be reviewed" if nothing changes.

questions.stem: What does the phrase "however frustrating" suggest about the office's view?
options: It doubts that the noise is as serious as the student has described
It accepts that the problem is real while maintaining that the rule does not cover it
It considers the student partly responsible for the noise in the building
It regards the rule on room changes as unfair to residents in his position
questions.explanation: The phrase concedes the student's frustration; the sentence still concludes that noise "does not ordinarily meet that standard".

questions.stem: According to the email, what will happen first?
options: The student will be offered a single room
The office will inspect Aldrich House
The resident adviser will talk to the neighbors
The student will complete a new request form
questions.explanation: "The resident adviser for your floor has been asked to speak with the students concerned this week."

stimulus.title: Memo — Department of History
stimulus.body:
The dean's office has confirmed that our travel allocation for the coming year will be the same as this year's. Since airfares and registration fees have risen by roughly a fifth, the same sum will not stretch as far.

Rather than reduce every award, the committee proposes to fund fewer trips at the current level. Priority would go to doctoral students presenting a paper for the first time and to faculty without external grants. Colleagues who hold such grants are asked, where the terms permit, to charge travel to them first. Comments on this proposal are welcome until May 15; absent strong objections, it will take effect in September.

questions.stem: Why does the memo say that the allocation "will not stretch as far"?
options: The budget is unchanged while the cost of each trip has increased
The dean's office has reduced the department's travel budget
More colleagues are expected to apply for travel support than before
External grants will no longer be allowed to cover travel costs
questions.explanation: The allocation "will be the same", but airfares and fees "have risen by roughly a fifth", so it pays for less.

questions.stem: Under the proposal, who would be least likely to receive departmental travel funds?
options: A professor with an external grant that allows travel costs
A doctoral student giving a first conference paper
A professor with no outside funding
A doctoral student whose paper has been accepted for the first time
questions.explanation: Priority goes to first-time doctoral presenters and "faculty without external grants"; grant holders are asked "to charge travel to them first".

stimulus.title: Research Ethics Office — Frequently Asked Questions
stimulus.body:
Do I need approval to interview people for a class project?
Not usually. Work carried out only to learn research methods, whose results will not be shared beyond the classroom, does not count as research under university policy. Your instructor is responsible for seeing that it is conducted properly.

What if I later want to publish the results?
Then the position changes. Approval cannot be granted retrospectively, so data collected without it may not be used in a thesis, article or public presentation. If there is any chance that your project will lead to publication, apply before you begin. An application that proves unnecessary costs you a few hours; missing approval can cost you the data.

questions.stem: According to the page, why does a typical class project not require approval?
options: The instructor has already obtained approval for the class
Interviews are exempt from university policy
Its purpose is training and its findings stay within the course
Students are not allowed to conduct real research
questions.explanation: Such work is done "only to learn research methods" and its results "will not be shared beyond the classroom", so it "does not count as research".

questions.stem: A student completed class interviews without approval and now wants to use them in her thesis. What does the page imply?
options: She can apply for approval now and then use the interviews
She may use them if her instructor confirms they were conducted properly
She may use them in the thesis but not in an article
She will have to collect new data after obtaining approval
questions.explanation: "Approval cannot be granted retrospectively, so data collected without it may not be used in a thesis."

questions.stem: What is the function of the final sentence of the page?
options: To warn students that applications are frequently rejected
To explain how long the approval process takes
To persuade students that applying early is the safer choice
To discourage students from publishing class projects
questions.explanation: It contrasts a small cost ("a few hours") with a large one ("can cost you the data") to support the advice "apply before you begin".

stimulus.title: Meridian Scholarship — Conditions of Renewal
stimulus.body: The scholarship is renewed each year provided that the holder completes at least 30 credits and maintains a grade average of 3.3 or above. A holder whose average falls between 3.0 and 3.3 is placed on probation for one term, during which payments continue; if the average for that term alone reaches 3.3, the scholarship is restored in full, and if not, it ends. An average below 3.0 ends the scholarship without probation. Holders who interrupt their studies for medical reasons may suspend the scholarship for up to two terms, during which no payments are made and no credits are required.

questions.stem: A holder finishes the year with 32 credits and an average of 3.1. What happens next?
options: She keeps receiving payments for one term while her results are reviewed
Her scholarship ends at once because her average is below 3.3
Her scholarship is renewed without conditions because she has 32 credits
Her payments are suspended until her average rises to 3.3 again
questions.explanation: An average "between 3.0 and 3.3" means probation "for one term, during which payments continue".

questions.stem: What must a holder on probation achieve for the scholarship to be restored?
options: An overall average of at least 3.3 for the whole year
At least 30 credits during the probation term
An average of at least 3.3 in the probation term itself
An average above 3.0 in the probation term
questions.explanation: The scholarship is restored "if the average for that term alone reaches 3.3".

stimulus.title: Summer Sublet — One Bedroom near the Science Campus
stimulus.body: Available June 1 to August 20. Furnished one-bedroom apartment on the third floor (no elevator), eight minutes on foot from the science campus. Rent is $780 a month, which covers water and internet; electricity is billed separately and has averaged $35 a month, though it runs higher when the air conditioner is in use. The lease forbids pets and smoking, and the landlord must approve any subtenant, which normally takes a week. I would prefer one person for the whole period but will consider two consecutive tenants if no gaps are left. A deposit of one month's rent is returned within ten days of departure.

stimulus.body:
Dear Ms. Aydin,

Thank you for sending us "Borrowed Voices". Both readers admired the ambition of the essay, and one called the opening pages the most arresting we received this cycle.

They were less persuaded by what follows. The argument of the second half leans heavily on a single interview, and the conclusion claims rather more than that evidence can carry. We cannot publish the piece as it stands.

We do not say this to everyone: should you wish to revise along these lines, we would read the essay again for the spring issue, though without any commitment on our part. The deadline is January 20.

With best wishes,
The Editors

questions.stem: What decision do the editors communicate?
options: They reject the current version but invite a revised one
They accept the essay provided the conclusion is shortened
They reject the essay and discourage resubmission
They postpone their decision until January 20
questions.explanation: "We cannot publish the piece as it stands", but if she revises "we would read the essay again for the spring issue".

questions.stem: What is the editors' principal criticism of the essay?
options: Its conclusions go beyond what its limited evidence supports
Its opening pages are weaker than the rest
It is too ambitious for an undergraduate journal
It relies on interviews instead of published sources
questions.explanation: The second half "leans heavily on a single interview", and the conclusion "claims rather more than that evidence can carry".

questions.stem: Why do the editors write "We do not say this to everyone"?
options: To warn her that the journal is highly selective
To apologize for the severity of their comments
To signal that the invitation to resubmit reflects real interest
To indicate that the readers disagreed with each other
questions.explanation: The remark introduces the offer to read a revision and marks it as an exception, not a routine courtesy.

stimulus.title: Office of the Registrar
stimulus.body: We have read the many comments on the new examination timetable, and we owe you a plainer explanation than the one we gave. Evening examinations were not introduced for anyone's convenience, least of all ours. The number of students entitled to extra time has doubled in four years, and the rooms suitable for them are few. Spreading examinations across more hours was the only way to avoid placing some students in corridors and offices, as happened last June. We recognize that a 7 p.m. paper is unwelcome. If your timetable now gives you three examinations within twenty-four hours, write to us and one will be moved.

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of the post?
options: To announce that evening examinations will be withdrawn
To apologize for errors in the published timetable
To ask students to stop commenting on the timetable
To justify an unpopular change and offer relief in the hardest cases
questions.explanation: The registrar gives "a plainer explanation" for evening examinations and offers to move one paper for students with three in twenty-four hours.

questions.stem: What does the post imply happened last June?
options: Evening examinations were tried for the first time
Several examinations had to be cancelled
Students complained about having three examinations in one day
Some students with extra time sat examinations in unsuitable places
questions.explanation: More hours were "the only way to avoid placing some students in corridors and offices, as happened last June", in a passage about students entitled to extra time and the few rooms suitable for them.

messages.text: Just finished the stack for section 4. Guess how many used the formula from the practice sheet on question 3.
Given that question 3 was deliberately written so that formula wouldn't work... all of them?
Twenty-two out of twenty-six. With total confidence. One even wrote "as shown in class."
Well, we did tell them the practice sheet was "representative." I'm starting to think that word did more harm than the exam.
I'm bringing it up Thursday. Either we stop handing out practice sheets or we write ones that don't all look alike.
I'd back the second. Taking them away just punishes the four who were paying attention.

questions.stem: What do the two assistants believe explains the students' mistake?
options: The students had not attended the classes where the topic was taught
Question 3 contained an error that made the formula seem to apply
The practice material led students to expect one type of problem
The formula had been explained incorrectly during the lectures
questions.explanation: Felix blames having called the practice sheet "representative", and Noor wants sheets "that don't all look alike".

questions.stem: What is Felix's attitude when he says the word "did more harm than the exam"?
options: Anger at the students for not thinking
Wry acknowledgment that the teaching team shares the blame
Satisfaction that the question worked as designed
Indifference to the results
questions.explanation: He says "we did tell them" and jokes that their own word caused the damage, which is self-critical irony.

questions.stem: Which course of action does Felix support?
options: Ending the distribution of practice sheets
Regrading question 3 for the whole section
Giving credit to the four students who answered correctly
Rewriting the practice sheets so that the problems vary
questions.explanation: Noor offers two options; Felix replies, "I'd back the second", that is, writing sheets "that don't all look alike".

stimulus.title: Memo — Use of Text-Generating Tools in Written Coursework
stimulus.body:
From September, each course outline must state which of three positions applies: such tools are prohibited, permitted with acknowledgment, or permitted freely. Where an outline is silent, the second position is deemed to apply.

The committee considered and rejected a single faculty-wide rule. What counts as legitimate assistance in a translation seminar differs from what counts in a course on argumentative writing, and instructors are better placed than we are to judge. We ask only that the position be justified to students in terms of what the assignment is meant to develop. A prohibition that cannot be explained in those terms is unlikely to be respected, and still less likely to be enforceable.

questions.stem: An instructor's course outline says nothing about text-generating tools. What follows?
options: Students may not use them at all
Students may use them without restriction
The instructor must ask the committee for a decision
Students may use them if they declare that they have done so
questions.explanation: "Where an outline is silent, the second position is deemed to apply", and the second position is "permitted with acknowledgment".

questions.stem: Why did the committee decide against a single rule for the whole faculty?
options: Appropriate use depends on what each course is trying to teach
Instructors had refused to accept a rule set by the committee
Students had asked for different rules in different departments
A rule for the whole faculty would have taken too long to agree on
questions.explanation: Legitimate assistance "differs" between a translation seminar and a writing course, and "instructors are better placed than we are to judge".
